correctness.rationale: The centered energy identity, global exponential stability for a>1/b, LaSalle attraction at a=1/b, and pointwise strict ceiling on each non-equilibrium bounded complete trajectory are correct. But the final claim additionally asserts that NO non-equilibrium compact invariant set can touch y=1/b. For (a,b,c)=(1/10,1/5,1), Q0=(0,5,0) and E+=(sqrt(39/50),11/10,-sqrt(39/50)) are distinct equilibria. The two-point set {Q0,E+} is compact, invariant and not a singleton equilibrium, yet intersects y=1/b at Q0. Thus the stated set-wide corollary is false; proof only excludes plane intersections by each non-equilibrium trajectory, not by arbitrary invariant sets containing the exceptional equilibrium. A surviving corrected statement would restrict compact invariant sets to ones disjoint from Q0, but no full corrected RESULT.md has been supplied, so the original claim is rejected.
